conflicts.point: Whether sub-second automated execution loops prevent meaningful human intervention or override before lethal force is applied.

positions.stance: Real-time battlefield monitoring networks and automated circuit breakers can catch and reverse anomalous targeting loops within 200 milliseconds.
Execution speeds under 200 milliseconds physically prevent human commanders from reviewing sensor feeds or executing meaningful interventions.

conflicts.point: Whether mandatory human oversight and bureaucratic rollback mechanisms serve as vital safety infrastructure or inefficient red tape.

positions.stance: Insisting on legacy bureaucratic reviews and human oversight for multi-billion-dollar software deployments causes preventable delays and increases overall casualties.
Modular rollback mechanisms and named human authorization structures are indispensable safeguards against cascading military escalation.

verdicts.conflict: Whether sub-second automated execution loops prevent meaningful human intervention or override before lethal force is applied.
verdicts.rationale: Human cognitive processing limits make sub-second review physically impossible. The skeptic position relies on well-documented neuroscientific limits of human reaction times, whereas the accelerationist claim about automated circuit breakers lacks verified combat telemetry.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Peer-reviewed operational telemetry from active combat zones proving that human commanders successfully intercept and reverse targeting loops within a 200-millisecond window.

verdicts.conflict: Whether mandatory human oversight and bureaucratic rollback mechanisms serve as vital safety infrastructure or inefficient red tape.
verdicts.rationale: The safetyist position accounts for legal liability under the Geneva Conventions and the risk of cascading escalation. The accelerationist argument narrowly frames software deployment as a commercial investment while ignoring international humanitarian law obligations.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Binding international legal reform that explicitly replaces individual criminal responsibility with corporate or algorithmic liability.
